title: Find your next question
brief: Define a relational database briefly as a system for representing related facts, querying and changing them, and enforcing specified integrity and transaction rules. Set up the order-reservation example, then expose direct task entrances before the walkthrough: first application to design, SQL and application integration; correctness incident to transactions; slow workload to execution and diagnosis; recovery preparation to operations; system evaluation to the root's shortlist section, following distribution only when its constraints matter. Name a concrete outcome for each path and make clear that the following walkthrough is the continuous first-reading route, not a prerequisite for revisiting one branch.

title: Put facts into relations and protect their meaning
brief: Show customers, orders, order lines and stock reservations as a small connected schema. Explain facts, keys and relationships through that example, and use one valid-quantity constraint to show a database-enforced rule. Establish that a schema expresses meaning, rather than being a collection of containers. Defer formal dependency analysis, SQL duplicates and missing-value semantics to their owning branches; introduce the shared-stock concurrency rule only in the transaction section.
